title: EBT lock controls can reduce future theft exposure while stolen benefits remain nonreplaceable
source_unit: Connecticut DSS EBT protection and stolen-benefit guidance
geography: Connecticut SNAP and cash-assistance EBT cardholders

denominator.unit: Connecticut EBT cardholders; statewide user count not disclosed

lock_control.value: Cardholders can lock and unlock EBT cards through MyDSS or the ConnectEBT app

out_of_state_control.value: Cardholders can block or unblock out-of-state transactions

replacement_boundary.value: Connecticut can replace a lost, stolen, or damaged card, but not SNAP or cash benefits stolen from the card

remaining_balance_transfer.value: Benefits left on the old card automatically transfer to the replacement card

observations.method: Structured extraction from current official Connecticut DSS EBT protection guidance; prevention controls, card replacement, account transfer, and nonreplacement of stolen benefits are retained as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: The public guidance does not disclose control uptake, prevented theft, stolen-benefit amounts, food-gap duration, benefit adequacy, appeal outcomes, trust, or later household security.
observations.subgroup: Connecticut SNAP and cash-assistance EBT cardholders; no statewide denominator or claimant-level follow-up is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: A cardholder-controlled lock can reduce exposure when used, but it shifts timing and attention requirements to the household while leaving an electronically stolen balance unrecovered under the stated rule.

related_sources.claim: Connecticut guidance says lost or stolen SNAP or Summer EBT benefits cannot be replaced, while a lost or stolen card itself can be replaced and remaining balances transfer.

Connecticut's EBT guidance distinguishes replacement of the physical card from replacement of stolen SNAP or cash benefits and describes the old-card deactivation and remaining-balance transfer route.

boundary: This record establishes Connecticut prevention controls and a physical-card replacement/account-transfer route alongside a stated nonreplacement boundary for stolen benefits. It does not establish control use, avoided theft, restored food access, adequacy, trust, or exit.
